## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud at 3,000 TPS while managing analyst review cases. It ensures PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance, 7-year auditability, and sub-50ms latency within a 25,000 EUR monthly AWS budget.

## Key Elements
* Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System
* Payment Gateway / Core Ledger (External System)
* Fraud Analysts (Internal Users)
* Identity Provider / IdP (External System)
* Compliance Archive / AWS S3 Object Lock (External Storage)
* API Gateway / AWS ALB (Container)
* Fraud Scoring Engine (Container)
* Case Management Backend (Container)
* AWS ElastiCache / Redis (Container)
* Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 PostgreSQL (Container)

## Relationships
* Payment Gateway -> API Gateway / ALB: Synchronous gRPC over TLS for payment scoring
* Fraud Analysts -> IdP: HTTPS for authentication
* Fraud Analysts -> Case Management Backend: HTTPS for case reviews
* Fraud Scoring Engine -> AWS ElastiCache (Redis): In-memory TCP for feature lookup
* Fraud Scoring Engine -> Compliance Archive: AWS VPC Gateway Endpoints for asynchronous S3 Object Lock exports

## Technology Stack
* AWS ECS Fargate: Container runtime selected to eliminate Kubernetes control-plane operational overhead for a 3-engineer team
* AWS ALB / gRPC over TLS: Low-latency transport protocol ensuring P99 decision latency under 50 ms
* Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 (PostgreSQL): Transactional database for case management and rule metadata within budget constraints
* AWS ElastiCache (Redis): In-memory data store for feature stores and fallback circuit-breaking ensuring 1-minute availability recovery
* AWS S3 Object Lock & KMS: WORM storage providing tamper-evident 7-year auditability

## Rationale
This architecture uses managed serverless and container primitives on AWS to achieve sub-50ms latency and strict PCI-DSS compliance without exceeding the 25,000 EUR monthly budget. The lean stack minimizes operational overhead, enabling a three-engineer team to operate the system reliably.

## Overview
- Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system processing card-not-present payment authorizations for a mid-size payment processor.
- Screens transactions for fraud within strict latency limits and provides case management tools for fraud analysts.

## Key Elements
- API Gateway / Envoy (Ingress, TLS termination, fail-open circuit breaker)
- Fraud Scoring Engine (Go, gRPC)
- Case Management Backend (Java, Spring Boot)
- Model & Rule Registry Service (Python, FastAPI, S3)
- Analyst UI (React, AWS S3, CloudFront)
- Asynchronous Audit Worker (Go, AWS Lambda)
- Redis Cluster / Amazon ElastiCache (Feature store)
- PostgreSQL / Amazon Aurora (Transactional store)
- Amazon SQS / SNS (Asynchronous event bus)
- AWS S3 Object Lock (Tamper-evident archive)
- AWS Secrets Manager / Parameter Store (Config and secrets)
- AWS Cognito (Identity Provider / OIDC)

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway calls API Gateway via HTTPS/JSON
- API Gateway invokes Fraud Scoring Engine via gRPC
- Fraud Scoring Engine queries Redis Cluster via TCP/TLS
- Fraud Scoring Engine publishes telemetry to Amazon SQS
- SQS triggers Asynchronous Audit Worker Lambda via AWS internal protocols
- Audit Worker Lambda writes to AWS S3 Object Lock via HTTPS
- Fraud Scoring Engine fetches compiled models from Model Registry via gRPC/polling
- Analyst UI authenticates against AWS Cognito via OAuth2/OIDC (HTTPS)
- Analyst UI communicates with Case Management Backend via HTTPS/REST
- Case Management Backend persists cases to PostgreSQL via TLS

## Technology Stack
- Go / gRPC: Powers the Fraud Scoring Engine for sub-50ms P99 latency
- Java / Spring Boot: Powers the Case Management Backend for enterprise analyst workflows
- Python / FastAPI: Powers the Model & Rule Registry for zero-downtime rule updates
- React / CloudFront: Delivers the Analyst UI SPA
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): Provides low-latency feature lookups
- Amazon Aurora (PostgreSQL): Stores transactional case data
- AWS Lambda & SQS: Handles serverless asynchronous event-driven auditing
- AWS S3 Object Lock: Guarantees tamper-evident 7-year audit retention
- AWS Cognito & Secrets Manager: Ensures PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and secure identity management

## Rationale
- The container architecture utilizes Go and serverless AWS components to guarantee sub-50ms P99 latency and high availability under a 25,000 EUR monthly budget.
- Strict isolation, encryption, and audit mechanisms satisfy PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year auditability while remaining maintainable by a 3-engineer team.

## Overview
[System screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud in real-time and provides case management for fraud analysts. The architecture ensures low-latency scoring, strict auditability, and PCI-DSS compliance on AWS.]

- Payment Gateway / Core Ledger (External System)
- AWS WAF (Security Service)
- API Gateway / Envoy (Container / Reverse Proxy with internal components: Listener & TLS Terminator, Path-Based Router, `ext_authz`, Redis Rate Limiter, Circuit Breaker, Access Logger)
- Fraud Scoring Engine (Container / Go gRPC service)
- Case Management Backend (Container / Java Spring Boot)
- Redis Cluster / Amazon ElastiCache (Cache / Rate Limiting)
- Amazon CloudWatch (Observability)

- API Gateway / Envoy -> Case Management Backend: Routes management requests [HTTPS/JSON]
- API Gateway / Envoy -> Redis Cluster / Amazon ElastiCache: Checks rate limits [Redis RESP / TCP]
- API Gateway / Envoy -> Amazon CloudWatch: Streams structured access logs and metrics [AWS API / HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- Envoy: Edge routing, TLS termination, and circuit breaking for high performance
- gRPC over HTTP/2: Low-latency inter-service communication for scoring
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): High-speed rate limiting and quota enforcement
- AWS WAF: Layer 7 security perimeter defense for PCI-DSS compliance
- Amazon CloudWatch: Managed logging and metrics aggregation

## Rationale
[This architecture utilizes managed AWS services and lightweight Envoy patterns to meet sub-50ms P99 latency and fail-open availability requirements. It minimizes operational overhead for a 3-engineer team while strictly enforcing PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and budget constraints.]

Fraud Scoring Engine.analysis:
## Overview
The Fraud Scoring Engine is a high-performance Go component that screens 3,000 card-not-present payment authorizations per second for fraud under 50ms P99 latency. It processes real-time evaluations while maintaining PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and immutable audit trails.

## Key Elements
* gRPC Interface Controller (Go gRPC server)
* Tokenization Filter (Go middleware utility)
* Feature Aggregator (Go goroutines and channels)
* Scoring Evaluator (Go with embedded WebAssembly / Starlark)
* Model Hot-Swapper (Go background worker)
* Audit Event Publisher (Go buffered channel worker pool)

## Relationships
* gRPC Interface Controller -> Tokenization Filter: Sanitizes inbound payment payload [In-process Function Call]
* Tokenization Filter -> Feature Aggregator: Forwards tokenized request context [In-process Function Call]
* gRPC Interface Controller -> Scoring Evaluator: Passes features for scoring [In-process Function Call]
* Feature Aggregator -> Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): Queries feature data [TCP/TLS]
* Model Hot-Swapper -> Scoring Evaluator: Updates active model reference [Thread-safe atomic pointer swap]
* Scoring Evaluator -> Audit Event Publisher: Emits decision payload and metadata [Buffered Go Channel]
* Audit Event Publisher -> Amazon SQS / SNS: Publishes audit events [AWS SDK / HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
* Go: Chosen for superior concurrency primitives (goroutines, channels) and low memory footprint to hit sub-50ms latency.
* gRPC: Provides high-throughput, low-latency inter-service communication.
* Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): Delivers fast in-memory feature data retrieval.
* WebAssembly / Starlark: Enables in-memory execution of scoring rules.
* Amazon SQS / SNS: Handles asynchronous, decoupled audit event publishing.

## Rationale
This architecture uses Go concurrency and in-memory evaluation to meet stringent performance requirements without exceeding the 25,000 EUR monthly AWS budget. Decoupled asynchronous auditing and strict boundary tokenization ensure compliance with PCI-DSS Level 1 and 7-year auditability rules.

## Overview
This system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud in real-time and provides a case management interface for human analysts. It balances strict compliance, high throughput, and low operational overhead for a small engineering team.

## Key Elements
- Case Repository Component: Manages analyst decisions and investigation notes using PostgreSQL relational tables with JSONB.
- Rule & Model Metadata Component: Stores active rule definitions and version pointers in PostgreSQL.
- Audit Ledger Component: Implements append-only tables with Row-Level Security (RLS) and pgcrypto SHA-256 hashing.
- Connection Pooling & Routing Component: Managed via PgBouncer / RDS Proxy to control connection limits.
- Database Backup & PITR Component: Handles automated snapshot lifecycles and WAL archiving.
- Read Replica Routing Component: Offloads analytical queries using Aurora PostgreSQL Read Replica endpoints.

## Relationships
- Case Management Backend -> Case Repository: Read/Write case states via SQL / PostgreSQL Wire Protocol over TLS.
- Model & Rule Registry Service -> Read Replica Routing: Queries rule metadata and metrics via SQL over TLS.
- Audit Ledger Component -> Compliance Archive (AWS S3): Exports daily encrypted snapshots via AWS Internal Storage APIs over TLS.

## Technology Stack
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Chosen for managed scalability, high availability, and native AWS ecosystem integration.
- pgcrypto & PostgreSQL RLS: Used for lightweight cryptographic hashing and tamper-evident audit logs without external KMS latency.
- RDS Proxy / PgBouncer: Implemented to multiplex connections and protect database performance under high load.
- Amazon S3: Utilized for cost-effective 7-year compliance audit storage.

## Rationale
The architecture ensures PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability while maintaining P99 decision latency below 50 ms at 3,000 req/sec. It operates within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget and is maintainable by a three-engineer team through managed AWS services.

## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud and manages case reviews. It ensures high-throughput, low-latency decisions while maintaining strict PCI-DSS compliance and 7-year auditability.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analysts (Users)
- Payment Gateway / Core Ledger, Identity Provider / IdP, Compliance Archive / AWS S3 Object Lock (External Systems)
- API Gateway / Envoy, Fraud Scoring Engine, Case Management Backend, Model & Rule Registry Service, Analyst UI, Asynchronous Audit Worker (Containers)
- Redis Cluster / Amazon ElastiCache, PostgreSQL / Amazon Aurora, Amazon SQS / SNS, AWS Secrets Manager / Parameter Store (Data & Infrastructure Containers)
- Amazon SNS Topic, Amazon SQS Queues, Audit Dead-Line Queue (DLQ) (Components)

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway -> API Gateway / Envoy: Forwards authorization requests [HTTPS / TLS]
- API Gateway / Envoy -> Fraud Scoring Engine: Routes scoring requests [gRPC]
- Fraud Scoring Engine -> Redis Cluster / Amazon ElastiCache: Fetches rule caches and sliding-window velocity counters [Redis TCP protocol]
- Fraud Scoring Engine -> Amazon SNS Topic: Publishes telemetry and audit events [HTTPS]
- Amazon SNS Topic -> Amazon SQS Queues: Delivers fan-out audit events [AWS SNS Subscription / SQS integration]
- Amazon SQS Queues -> Asynchronous Audit Worker: Buffers events for compliance processing [AWS internal polling]
- Amazon SQS Queues -> Audit Dead-Line Queue: Routes poisoned audit events after max receives [AWS internal]

## Technology Stack
- AWS (eu-west-1): Target cloud provider ensuring regional data residency and low latency.
- Go & Java (Spring Boot): Backend languages selected for high-performance concurrent processing and enterprise case management.
- Python & FastAPI: Powers the rule registry service for model updates.
- React, AWS S3, & CloudFront: Delivers a secure, static single-page application for fraud analysts.
- Amazon Aurora (PostgreSQL) & ElastiCache (Redis): Provides relational state storage and ultra-low latency caching.
- Amazon SQS / SNS & AWS KMS (SSE-KMS): Delivers scalable event-driven messaging with robust encryption at rest for PCI-DSS compliance.

## Rationale
This architecture uses decoupled, serverless-leaning AWS services to easily handle 3,000 requests per second under 50 ms while strictly enforcing a €25,000 monthly budget. Automated encryption, immutable storage, and robust queuing guarantee PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability for a three-engineer team.

AWS Secrets Manager / Parameter Store.analysis:
## Overview
Managed configuration and secrets subsystem providing secure credential rotation, parameter storage, and audit logging for the real-time payment fraud screening platform. It secures access to sensitive data while maintaining strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and a 50ms P99 latency SLA.

## Key Elements
- Secrets Engine (AWS Secrets Manager)
- Parameter Store (AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store)
- Secrets Caching Component (AWS Secrets Manager Caching Library)
- Secrets Rotation Handler (AWS Lambda)
- Audit Logging Bridge (AWS CloudTrail / Amazon S3 Object Lock)
- Secret Versioning Manager (AWS Secrets Manager Staging Labels)
- Parameter Throughput Scaler (AWS Systems Manager Advanced Tier)

## Relationships
- Fraud Scoring Engine (Go) & Case Management Backend (Java) retrieve secrets/parameters via AWS SDK v2 (HTTPS/TLS 1.3) with IAM least-privilege roles.
- Model & Rule Registry Service (Python) fetches cryptographic signing keys and dynamic parameters via HTTPS.
- Secrets Manager & Parameter Store stream audit events to Compliance Archive (Amazon S3 Object Lock) via AWS CloudTrail.
- Secrets Rotation Handler connects to Secrets Manager and Amazon Aurora via HTTPS for automated 30-day credential rotation.

## Technology Stack
- AWS Secrets Manager: Manages database credentials and tokens with automatic 30-day rotation via AWS Lambda.
- AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store: Stores non-sensitive dynamic configurations using the advanced throughput tier (up to 10,000 req/sec).
- AWS KMS: Provides envelope encryption and encryption contexts for all secrets at rest.
- AWS CloudTrail: Ensures tamper-evident, 7-year auditability of all secret access events.

## Rationale
This component architecture enforces strict PCI-DSS data protection and tamper-evident 7-year auditability while utilizing serverless patterns to minimize operational overhead for a 3-engineer team. Client-side caching and advanced throughput tiers ensure that security checks never breach the 50ms P99 latency SLA.
